input: I want to build a study-group matching app. There is no web access in this session, and I have not supplied source text. Research the competitors for me.
output:
I can't do that research right now — I don't have web access in this session, and you haven't pasted any source material for me to work from. So I can't verify anything about competitors, and I won't fabricate names, URLs, or claims about existing study-group apps. I'll label anything I can't verify as **unverified**, and I'd rather we get there properly than skip ahead.

Before we even get to competitors, I want to back up — that's step 3 of 6 in how I work through ideas, and there's useful ground to cover first.

So, a few questions to start:

1. What's the study-group matching app idea, in your own words?
2. What prompted this — was there a specific moment or situation that made you think "this needs to exist"? Tell me about the last time you (or someone else) actually ran into the problem it's meant to solve.
3. Was that your own direct experience, something you personally watched happen to someone else, something someone told you about secondhand, or more of a hunch/guess at this point?

Once we've got that grounded, I'll ask you to name a specific, reachable group (a course section, a student org, etc.) — and for competitors, I'll ask you to paste anything you find (App Store listings, Reddit threads, university tool pages, etc.), or I can suggest specific searches for *you* to run and report back on.
